svg.title: The public dates of CVE-2026-98432, the Linux kernel flaw Anthropic's model wrote an exploit for, from 25 September to 10 November 2026, with its report date unknown
svg.desc: A vertical timeline, to scale from 25 September 2026. Above it, off the scale, the report: no public source we read dates it, so it is not placed. 25 September: the CVE number reserved. 1 October: the fix's author date; when the fix was first public isn't dated. 11 October: the first stable kernels with the fix, 6.18.56 and 7.2.10. 15 October: the CVE published, and five more stable kernels released. 24 October: the release date on the four earliest SUSE advisory pages we followed that name the flaw, shown hollow because what it marks isn't stated. 27 October: Anthropic's post describing the exploit, in prose with no code. 29 October: SUSE announces those four advisories on its public list, and eight more on 3 November. 30 October, in UTC: the first oss-security message whose subject names the CVE, forwarding Go's announcement. 1 November: Red Hat's earliest errata we followed. 10 November: Ubuntu's earliest notice. Debian's fixes were in place by our first read on 1 November, but its pages give no dates. Each date is on its own source's clock, as UTC days. Sources: kernel.org stable changelogs, the CVE record, SUSE's advisory pages and announcement list, Anthropic's post, the oss-security archive, Red Hat's and Ubuntu's trackers, read by Lighthouse from 16 to 21 November 2026.
